audit.title: Tokenized Equity Feeds

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Sections open with liftable definitions: "Tokenized equities are blockchain tokens that represent ownership or economic exposure to traditional stocks and ETFs." Risk sections lead with the risk, then mitigate. Minor weakness: the H1 body defers to a `<TokenizedEquityFeeds>` component that renders nothing in the served text.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. 37 sections, median 58 words, max 390, no section over 600 words, two tables, 72 bullets. Near-ideal chunk boundaries.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Adequate. Real specifics exist (24/5, 6.5 hours, session hour ranges, 2x/10x split moves), but qualitative filler dilutes them: "high fidelity," "intelligent smoothing," "various trading venues." Only 3 of 59 numerals carry units.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 12 links, all internal, zero external/primary sources. Claims about NYSE/NASDAQ hours, consolidated tape, and corporate-action mechanics are unattributed to any authoritative source.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Strong. "Chainlink Tokenized Equity Feeds provide continuous 24/5 pricing for tokenized representations of US equities and ETFs" is a clean verbatim-liftable canonical statement.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Poor. Measured: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, datePublished/dateModified absent, no og/twitter tags, no head metadata captured. This is the largest scored deficit.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 0 fenced code blocks. The pause-confirmation math is inline prose (`new multiplier × current equity price`); there is no snippet showing how to actually read the feed or implement the staleness/value-bound checks the page repeatedly prescribes.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Good. FAQ, risks, mitigations, best practices, and integration-testing lifecycle are all present. Weakness: risk headings are concept-titled ("Limited provider coverage…"), not symptom-titled ("Why does my feed return zero?"), so symptom queries miss.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Consistent entity naming ("Chainlink Tokenized Equity Feeds"), unambiguous prose. Docked only for residual vague quantifiers (various, significant, quickly).

audit.summary: This is a well-structured conceptual and risk-reference page for Chainlink Tokenized Equity Feeds, with clean H2/H3/H4 hierarchy (37 headings, zero level skips), strong answer-first definitions, and two useful comparison tables. Its single biggest strength is scannable chunking — every risk carries a self-contained explanation plus a Mitigation block that a RAG engine can lift whole. Its biggest opportunity is machine-readability: the served HTML has zero JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and no visible last-updated date, all of which suppress agent trust and entity resolution. Secondary gaps are the absence of any runnable code (a data-feeds page with no read example) and symptom-phrased headings that would catch the queries developers actually type.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and visible last-updated date
recommendations.change: Emit a `TechArticle` JSON-LD block with `headline`, `about` ("Chainlink Data Feeds", "Tokenized Equities"), `dateModified`, and a self-referential `canonical`; surface a visible "Last updated" line under the H1.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent parseability and E-E-A-T trust; a missing canonical risks dilution across the `.md` and HTML variants.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased subheadings to the risk sections
recommendations.where: "Limited provider coverage…", "Weekend and holiday behavior", "Market closures and halts…"
recommendations.issue: Concept-titled headings miss symptom queries the content already answers.
recommendations.change: Add H4s or lead sentences phrased as queries: "Why does my tokenized equity feed return a price of zero?", "Why is my feed stale over the weekend?", "Why did the feed price jump at session close?" — each answering in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: Developers and agents query by symptom/error, not concept name; the answers exist verbatim in body text but lose retrieval to the concept-titled headings.

recommendations.title: Add a runnable read + validation snippet
recommendations.where: new subsection under "Best practices → Protocol design" or after "About tokenized equity feeds"
recommendations.issue: 0 fenced code blocks on a feed page that repeatedly prescribes staleness and value-bound checks.
recommendations.change: Add a tagged, complete Solidity (and/or JS) snippet reading `latestRoundData()`, checking `updatedAt` staleness, and enforcing min/max bounds plus a zero-value reject — the exact mitigations named in prose.
recommendations.why: Agents completing integration tasks lift copy-pasteable code; a snippet turns abstract mitigations into an extractable, actionable unit.

recommendations.title: Add external primary-source citations
recommendations.where: session-hours table, "Weekend and holiday behavior", "Corporate actions"
recommendations.issue: Measured — "0 external, 0 to primary sources"; NYSE/NASDAQ hours and calendars are unattributed.
recommendations.change: Inline-link NYSE/NASDAQ official trading-hours and holiday-calendar pages, and the consolidated-tape (SIP) reference, where those facts are stated.
recommendations.why: Inline links to canonical primary sources raise credibility and citation rate; the page currently asserts market facts without attribution.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers with concrete values
recommendations.where: "How tokenized equity feeds work", session-aware smoothing
recommendations.change: Quantify where possible ("converges within seconds to tens of seconds" is already used elsewhere — reuse it; name venue count or source it), or drop the qualifier.
recommendations.why: Quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes; qualitative-only prose underperforms in extraction.

recommendations.title: Populate the "Available tokenized equity feeds" section
recommendations.issue: "The following table shows all available tokenized equity feeds." — no table renders in served text.
recommendations.change: Render the feed table inline (asset, issuer, network, address, heartbeat) or, if dynamic, state the exact count and link the Provider Catalog in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: A heading promising a table but delivering none is an unresolved reference; a filled table adds high-value liftable specifics.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers present (measured): "various", "significant", "quickly" — surgical replacements above.

Unrendered component reference under H1 (`<TokenizedEquityFeeds section="tokenizedEquityNote" />`) and an empty promised table under "Available tokenized equity feeds" — both are unresolved cross-references in the served text.
No stale-content flag, but freshness is *unverifiable* (no dateModified) — treat as a metadata gap, not staleness.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; verify this page is enumerated in it.
Site-level JSON-LD/schema and canonical strategy should be applied consistently across `data-feeds/*`; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` so metadata can be fully verified rather than inferred absent.
Earned citations from DeFi-integration and RWA aggregator pages would raise retrieval authority — off-page, not scored here.
